lines.text: # Faculty of Arts — Building Plan (Footprint, Zoning and Finalized Materials)
**Stage:** university-plan (post-survey, all six faculty surveys read)
**Site:** flat, level ground, ~60 m × 60 m (≈3,600 m²); stratified (layered) soil,
generally suitable for standard shallow spread-footing foundations.
**Brief:** lecture halls/classrooms for a mid-sized faculty, staff offices, and a
cafeteria/canteen serving students and staff.
This plan finalizes the footprint/zoning and the material choices for the Arts
building, in particular the cafeteria. It is built on my own survey
(`SURVEY_ARTS.md`) and on the five peer surveys, which I have now read in full.
Section 5 states explicitly what a peer's survey changed and what it did not.
## 1. Site strategy (finalized)
The site facts are unchanged from my survey: flat, level, layered soil. The two
governing risks remain **water** (a level site cannot shed water by fall) and
**differential settlement** (bearing capacity is not uniformity on a layered
profile). Both are carried into this plan as design requirements, not deferred
details.
**Foundations (final).** Shallow reinforced-concrete pad footings under columns
and strip footings under load-bearing walls, founded on the verified bearing
stratum, tied together by a **reinforced ground-beam / tie-beam grid**. A
**borehole / trial-pit grid across the whole footprint** — not one central hole —
is a precondition of the foundation design, and must include the cafeteria
corner. Column bases are kept on a single stratum where possible; where a
stratum transition crosses the footprint, footings are stepped or deepened
across it. A **stiffened strip or raft** is held in reserve for the spine and any
bay that cannot avoid a transition. Ground-floor slabs and drainage are detailed
to tolerate small differential movement (movement joints, flexible service
connections, reinforcement detailed for it). No piling is anticipated.
**Drainage and levels (final).** The building is raised on a **plinth with
finished floor level 450–600 mm above surrounding external ground** (raised from
the 150 mm minimum in my survey — see §5), with a graded perimeter apron and a
fall away from the building on all sides. Stormwater is collected by a perimeter
land-drain / French drain plus a positive piped system to the site outfall;
